partially_covered.missing: Ontology does not explicitly model all organization details (e.g., contact info, registration numbers); only addresses and GLN are covered.
Item information is limited to net price and quantity; lacks detailed item attributes (e.g., description, product code).

cq_coverage.details: Most CQs are covered by structured classes and properties. Partial gaps for organization and item detail properties. No CQs are completely missing.

strengths: Deep hierarchy (Envelope > Message > InvoiceMessage > Section > Subsections)
Advanced use of restrictions and equivalence axioms
weaknesses: No explicit disjoint union axioms for Section subclasses

likely_oops_pitfalls: P4: Missing domain or range for some properties (minor risk, but most covered)
P7: Lack of explicit disjoint unions for Section subclasses
reasoner_risks: Hermit/Pellet may struggle with deeply nested restrictions if instances are complex, but no datatype violations detected

improvement_suggestions.suggestion: Expand Organization and Item classes with additional data properties (e.g., organization contact info, item description, product code) to fully answer CQ5 and CQ8.
improvement_suggestions.expected_impact: Complete coverage for queries about detailed organization and item information.

improvement_suggestions.suggestion: Add owl:disjointUnionOf axioms for Section subclasses (HeaderSection, DetailSection, SummarySection) to clarify structural constraints.
improvement_suggestions.expected_impact: Improved logical clarity and validator compatibility.

improvement_suggestions.suggestion: Introduce more general class axioms, e.g., for AgentRoleAssignment, to capture multi-role scenarios and ensure completeness in role modeling.
Add domain-specific annotation properties (e.g., skos:definition, skos:example) for improved documentation.

summary: The ontology provides deep hierarchical structure, rich axiomatization, and broad coverage for EDIFACT invoice scenarios. Minor gaps exist in item and organization detail modeling, but overall constraint adherence and OWL 2 compliance are excellent. Validator and reasoner compatibility is high, with only minor risks. Recommended improvements will further strengthen CQ coverage and logical clarity.
